changes.new: Over $1,000, furnished for signature before work starts; states total cost with parts and materials listed, any charge for an estimate, and the business name and address (815 ILCS 513/15)
changes.support: Prior to initiating home repair or remodeling work for over $1,000, a person engaged in the business of home repair or remodeling shall furnish to the customer for signature a written contract or work order that states the total cost, including parts and materials listed with reasonable particularity and any charge for an estimate. In addition, the contract shall state the business name and address of the person engaged in the business of home repair or remodeling.

changes.new: Three business days (815 ILCS 505/2B); age 65 or older with an uninvited solicitor, sold at the home: 15 full business days (815 ILCS 513/22)
changes.support: A person age 65 or older who purchases home repair or remodeling services from an uninvited solicitor may cancel any contract with a person engaged in home repair or remodeling by notifying that person within 15 full business days following the day on which the contract was signed if the agreement for the home repair or remodeling was made at the home of the purchaser.

changes.new: Age 65 or older, uninvited solicitor, agreement made at the purchaser's home: 15 full business days (815 ILCS 513/22). The 505/2B statement and form still say three business days.
changes.support: A person age 65 or older who purchases home repair or remodeling services from an uninvited solicitor may cancel any contract with a person engaged in home repair or remodeling by notifying that person within 15 full business days following the day on which the contract was signed if the agreement for the home repair or remodeling was made at the home of the purchaser.

changes.new: Disclosure in the contract and consent before charging; written notice 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline for terms of 12 months or more that renew for more than one month
changes.support: where such contract term is a specified term of 12 months or more, and where such contract automatically renews for a specified term of more than one month unless the consumer cancels the contract, shall notify the consumer in writing of the automatic renewal. Written notice shall be provided to the consumer no less than 30 days and no more than 60 days before the cancellation deadline

changes.new: OFFICIAL text read at ilga.gov; covers a written consumer contract that auto-renews; no small-business or service-type exemption
changes.support: No small-business or service-type exemption appears; exemptions are business-to-business contracts, banks, utilities under Article XXII, insurance-regulated parties.

unsure: IL-pamphlet: the pamphlet is a separate handout, not contract text, and the Attorney General's printed pamphlet differs from the statutory text; which to hand out is open.
IL-lien: it is unclear whether the notice should be printed in the contract or given as a separate statement before first payment; the statute allows either.
IL-arbitration-margin: no wording is prescribed, but the margin accept or reject mark is a signing step the contract may need to leave room for.
IL-insurance-cancel: the statement and form are in the contract only for insurance-paid jobs; the builder cannot tell whether a job is insurance-paid.
The state file says roofing contracts must show the Illinois roofing license name and number (513/18(d)); the license field was left unchanged because it is roofing only.

IL-pamphlet is stored on file only: the statute says the pamphlet must be a separate document in at least 12 point type, and the file says the Attorney General's printed pamphlet is worded differently from the statutory text.

IL-lien and IL-insurance-cancel/-form are stored on file, not printed, because the builder cannot tell owner-occupied single-family or insurance-paid jobs; if Nicole prefers to print IL-lien for every residential contract (the statute allows it in the contract), the range is already cut.
